BASE.name: ATTACK_VECTOR
BASE.justification: The vulnerability is triggered through user-controlled input that influences internal request URLs or page references over application network flows.

BASE.name: ATTACK_COMPLEXITY
BASE.justification: Exploitation is straightforward when unvalidated input is concatenated into resource identifiers without proper sanitization.

BASE.name: PRIVILEGES_REQUIRED
BASE.justification: An authenticated user with access to the vulnerable functionality can often supply the malicious input needed to exploit the issue.

BASE.name: USER_INTERACTION
BASE.justification: No additional user interaction is required once the attacker can submit crafted input to the vulnerable code path.

BASE.name: SCOPE
BASE.justification: The impact remains within the same application and trust boundary that processes the unsafe resource identifier.

BASE.name: CONFIDENTIALITY
BASE.justification: Improper control of resource identifiers can expose internal endpoints, sensitive records, or unintended resources to unauthorized access.

BASE.name: INTEGRITY
BASE.justification: Attackers may manipulate requests or target unintended internal resources, resulting in unauthorized actions or data modification.

BASE.name: AVAILABILITY
BASE.justification: Resource misuse may cause limited disruption or unintended processing, but availability is typically a secondary concern.

TEMPORAL.name: EXPLOIT_CODE_MATURITY
TEMPORAL.justification: Unsafe URL or resource construction vulnerabilities are easy to demonstrate with crafted inputs.

TEMPORAL.name: REMEDIATION_LEVEL
TEMPORAL.justification: The standard remediation is to validate, sanitize, or safely transform untrusted input before using it in resource identifiers.

TEMPORAL.name: REPORT_CONFIDENCE
TEMPORAL.justification: The weakness is well understood, maps directly to CWE-99, and is reliably identified by static analysis.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_ATTACK_VECTOR
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: In the deployed environment, the vulnerable resource construction remains reachable through application network interfaces.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_ATTACK_COMPLEXITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Environmental conditions do not significantly increase the difficulty of exploiting unsafe resource identifiers.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_PRIVILEGES_REQUIRED
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Typical authenticated access is still sufficient to reach the vulnerable functionality in most deployments.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_USER_INTERACTION
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: The vulnerability remains exploitable without requiring action from another user.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_SCOPE
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: The impact remains within the same application or organizational security boundary.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_CONFIDENTIALITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: In production environments, unintended access to internal resources or endpoints may expose sensitive business or platform data.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_INTEGRITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Manipulated resource identifiers may trigger unauthorized internal actions or alter the behavior of trusted workflows.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: MODIFIED_AVAILABILITY
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Availability impact remains limited, though misuse of internal resources may degrade operations or trigger unintended requests.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: CONFIDENTIALITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Protecting internal endpoints, resource references, and associated data is critical in most enterprise environments.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: INTEGRITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Preventing unauthorized manipulation of internal request targets and resulting actions is a high priority.

ENVIRONMENTAL.name: AVAILABILITY_REQUIREMENT
ENVIRONMENTAL.justification: Availability matters because abuse of internal resources can affect workflows, though confidentiality and integrity remain more critical.
